Simultaneously forming a carbon–carbon and a carbon–heteroatom bond in a single step through transition metal-catalyzed
alkene difunctionalization strategy has emerged as a powerful tool for synthetic organic chemistry. Due to the uncontrollable
reactivity, direct cross-coupling with bromoallenes as the building blocks for the selective allenation and borylation remains
challenging. We herein report a new type ofS- andP-stabilized bromoallenes for palladium-catalyzed modular allenation and
borylation of alkenes to the divergent synthesis of multiply functionalized allenes in a highly regio- and diastereoselective
manifold.Thereactionfeaturesbroadsubstratescopeandwidefunctionalgroupcompatibility,thusprovidingastraightforward
method to install allenyl and boryl groups across alkenes. Control experiments highlight the crucial importance ofS-, P-
stabilizationfortheoxidativeinsertionofPd-speciesintotheallenyl–Brbond.Thefacilesynthesesofbioactiveallenicsteroids
and exocyclic allenes demonstrate the synthetic utility of this protocol.

1 Introduction
Polyfunctionalized allenes are very important building
blocksinorganictransformations [1–3]andmaterialscience
[4,5] due to their unique orthogonal cumulative π-systems.
Many efforts have been made toward their syntheses by
developing efficient and practical methodologies during the
last decades[6–8]. Among them, multi-functionalized and
exocyclicallenesbearingvaluablefunctionalgroups,suchas
halides, sulfones, and phosphines, are highly desirable units
and widely present in natural products [9,10], bioactive
molecules [11,12], chiral phosphine ligands [13,14], and
catalysts (Scheme 1a) [15]. Hence, there is a continued
strong demand for the efficient and selective synthesis of
such scaffolds in a diverse fashion.
Thus far, catalytic substitution reactions with propargylic
derivatives [16–20] and remote double functionalization of
1,3-enynes have recognized as the synthetic tools for af-
fording allenes with one or two synthetically useful func-
tional groups[21–25]. On the other hand, transition-metal-
catalyzed1,2-difunctionalizationofunactivatedalkeneswith
two different functional groups has been recognized as an
increasingly versatile tool for the synthesis of highly com-
plex molecules [26–30]. The bench-stable bromoallenes

with a bromoallene, thein situ formed alkylmetal species
would be coupled with a suitable nucleophile. However,
severalmajorchallengesstillneedtobeovercome:(1)while
avoiding both C=C insertion and radical tautomerization of
bromoallenes, the transition metal must selectively undergo
oxidative addition into the allenyl–Br bond; (2) controlling
the regioselectivity and diastereoselectivity; (3) β-H elim-
ination of the Csp

(Scheme 1b).
Very recently, Zhuet al. [37,38] disclosed a new type of
allenyl bromide bearing alkenyl sulfone moieties for the
radical-mediated 1,2-alkynylalkenylation and 1,2-en-
ynylalkenylation of alkenes in the presence of photocatalyst
under irradiation. Here, the sulfone group is critically im-
portant not only as a linker for intramolecular radical mi-
gration, but also for stabilizing the initial allenyl radical.
Notably, the reformed allenyl radicalI undergoes a facile
tautomerization process, thus achieving sequential installa-
tion of alkynyl and alkenyl groups across alkenes (Scheme
1c). Beyond that, the process consisting of highly selective
C=C insertion of bromoallene, along with a subsequent β-
elimination affording a propargylic compound was also ob-
servedinmanganese-catalyzeddirectC–Hpropargylationof
indoles [39]. These results suggested that the bromoallenes
were preferential transferred into propargyl and alkynyl
functionalities. As such, a practical approach for the con-
structionofanewfunctionalizedallenes viapreciseallenyl–
Br bond activation is highly desirable.
With this purpose in mind, we became interested in de-
veloping an efficient alkene difucntionalization to the di-
vergentsynthesisofdecoratedalleneswithbromoallenes.In
order to stabilize thein situ formed allenyl-Pd intermediate,
we herein designed and prepared a range of practical and
bench-stable S- and P-stabilized bromoallenes, specifically
for modular palladium-catalyzed allenylborylation of un-
activated alkenes. Indeed, various bromoallenes bearing
sulfones, phosphines and trifluoromethyl moieties react

By the use of the sulfonyl-stabilized bromoallenes (2) as

toaffordthecorrespondingproducts 4–6 viaselectiveβ,γ-,γ,

bearingmethyl,ethyl,andphenylgroupssmoothlydelivered
the desired allenes 7–9 with moderate to good yields and
excellent diastereoselectivity. Additionally, unsymmetrical
olefins containing the more hindered aliphatic substituents
bearing chloro, double bond, ester and phthaloyl-protected
amine functional groups were well-tolerated under the re-
action conditions, giving the polyfunctionalized allenes10–
13 in 50%–89% yields with complete control of diastereos-
electivity. Remarkably, the allenylborylation also smoothly
occurred for substrates containing sterically hindered α-
substituents (14–24). A variety of valuable electrophilic
functional groups, such as cyclopropyl (17), trifluoromethyl
(19and 20),chloro(18),bromo(21),nitrile(22),andalkenes
(23, 24) were well-tolerated by the palladium catalytic sys-

yields with high diastereoselectivity. For γ,δ-unsaturated

Inspired by the success of our palladium-catalyzed sub-
sequential allenylborylation of unsaturated aliphatic acid
derivatives, we became intrigued by examining the possibi-
lityfordirectallenationofalkenylamineswiththeassistance
of picolinamide auxiliary (Scheme 2b)[47–49]. Terminal
homo- and bishomoallylamines were initially tested and
deliveredthecorrespondingallenylatedamines 38and 39 via
five- or six-membered palladacycles. Both internal alkeny-
lamines and terminal alkenylamines bearing an alkyl-sub-
stituent at the α-position proceeded in excellent regio- and
diastereoselective fashion, affording 40–44 in 55%–87%
yields. Likewise, the allenation of alkenylamines also ex-
hibited high generality toward various exocyclic bro-
moallenes, thereby providing an expedient route to access
aminoboryl-functionalized exoallenes45–49 in moderate to
good yields, as well as high diastereoselectivity.
Onthe basisoftheremarkablyhigh efficacyofthe alkene
allenation with S-stabilized bromoallenes, we further in-
vestigated analogous allenylborylation of unactivated al-
kenes with differentP-stabilized bromoallenes (Scheme 3).
It is noteworthy that both phosphonate and phosphine oxide
substituted bromoallenes were well-tolerated by palladium
catalyst, successfully undergoing cascade allenylborylation
and forming the synthetically useful allenyl phosphorous
compounds 50–56 in a modular fashion. Moreover, the
electron-deficient trifluoromethyl-substituted bromoallene
wasfoundtobeaviablesubstrateaswell,albeitwitharather
modest yield of product57.
Regarding the reaction mechanism, a series of control
experiments with stoichiometric quantities of representative
radical scavengers, such as 2,2,6,6-tetramethyl-1-piper-
inedinyloxy (TEMPO), butylated hydroxytoluene (BHT),
and 1,1-diphenylethene, were performed. The allenylbor-
ylation product 4 was obtained with negligibly reduced
yields under the described conditions (Scheme 4a). These
results strongly indicate that the reaction undergoes a non-
radical process. Importantly, we also examined the envi-
sioned alkene allenylborylation with differently substituted
amides.Thepresenceofabidentatedirectinggroup,suchas
8-aminoquinoline or 2-methylthioaniline, was proven to be
crucially important for activating the palladium catalyst and
promoting the regioselective allenylation and borylation
(Scheme 4b). Intrigued by the unique effects of α-function-
alities of bromoallenes, we prepared the bromoallenes
bearing different α-substituents and performed the parallel
experiments under the identical reaction conditions. No re-

modularallenylborylation,wefurthersynthesizedtheallenic

excellent yield by our simple catalytic system. These results

3 Conclusions
Inconclusion,wehavereportedthepreparationof S-and P-
stabilized bromoallenes, which proceeded oxidative inser-
tion of Pd-species into allenyl–Br bond to form the key al-
lenyl–Pd intermediates, thereby achieving modular
allenation and borylation of unactivated alkenes in a regio-,
site-, and diastereoselective fashion. Control experiments
highlighted the crucial importance of theS- andP-conjuga-
tion for enhancing the reactivity of bromoallenes, as well as
the unique directing and ligand-tuning effects of bidentate
groups for ensuring chemo- and diastereoselectivity. More-
over,thesyntheticutilityofouralkeneallenylborylationwas
well-illustrated by the facile syntheses of bioactive allenic
steroids and derivatizations of the resulting allenes. We be-
lieve this work will open a perspective for the modular
preparation of multi-functionalized allenes and find wide
applications in allene chemistry.
